bug_semantics: For a window drawable, do_get_buffers allocated only count + 1 DRI2BufferPtr slots, filled count client-requested slots, and then used arithmetic attachment counters to decide whether to append implicit front buffers. With at least two DRI2BufferBackLeft requests and one DRI2BufferFrontLeft request, need_real_front remained positive even though FrontLeft was already present, so a redundant real-front pointer was appended at buffers[count]. The FrontLeft request also made need_fake_front positive, so the fake-front pointer was then written at buffers[count + 1], one pointer beyond the heap allocation. The DRI2GetBuffers and DRI2GetBuffersWithFormat request paths both called this helper, allowing a local X client to crash the server or potentially escalate privileges when it ran as root.
flaw_origin: Commit ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 replaced the parent's bulk CreateBuffers path with per-attachment allocation and introduced need_real_front++/-- alongside the existing fake-front accounting, while retaining an allocation sized for only one implicit attachment. The parent could append at most one fake front and therefore respected its count + 1 capacity; the new combination could append both a redundant real front and a fake front. Treating attachment presence as signed counts rather than boolean presence broke the allocation invariant.

It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI attribution marker.
evidence: First-party X.Org advisory https://lists.x.org/archives/xorg-announce/2026-June/003702.html identifies the DRI2 DRIGetBuffers/DRIGetBuffersWithFormat out-of-bounds write, the multiple-BackLeft plus one-FrontLeft trigger, fixed releases xorg-server-21.1.23 and xwayland-24.1.12, and fixes 339c279514326134b0878fc23ce6e9520440ce7f and b7aa65cc3bb11b792ce2a3f511ba9b863acb11c8. `git show b7aa65cc3bb11b792ce2a3f511ba9b863acb11c8 -- hw/xfree86/dri2/dri2.c` shows the direct repair: replace need_real_front/need_fake_front arithmetic with boolean presence tests so no more than count + 1 slots are accessed; its message explicitly says `Fixes: ff6c7764c290`. `git show 339c279514326134b0878fc23ce6e9520440ce7f` shows the immediately following defense-in-depth change, whose parent is b7aa65cc3bb11b792ce2a3f511ba9b863acb11c8, deduplicating attachments and bounding attachment values/count. `git log -L 580,650:hw/xfree86/dri2/dri2.c b7aa65cc3bb11b792ce2a3f511ba9b863acb11c8^` reaches ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 and shows that it added the count + 1 pointer allocation, need_real_front++/--, and both post-loop appends. `git log --all --reverse -S 'need_real_front++' -- hw/xfree86/dri2/dri2.c` likewise identifies ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 as the original mainline writer; 4fad615d689c61c6c3a000295a1fa755359737cb is the later stable-branch backport/carrier, not the original BIC. Direct parent-tree inspection with `git show 28ddfc88d8d547941c7f4713db527a3c2f9ec35a:hw/xfree86/dri2/dri2.c` and `git grep need_real_front 28ddfc88d8d547941c7f4713db527a3c2f9ec35a` confirms no need_real_front state or second append in the parent; it only had capacity-safe fake-front insertion. Version checks show stable carrier 4fad615d689c61c6c3a000295a1fa755359737cb in xorg-server-1.6.1.902 and xorg-server-1.6.2, canonical BIC ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 in xorg-server-21.1.22, and vulnerable `need_real_front++` at hw/xfree86/dri2/dri2.c:607 in that tag. xorg-server-21.1.23 instead contains security backports 4926348d826b7dc12d51d7e41bd9068aee5f90af and f0b8e6e1d969548c0625051d56a780e5df39de26 and the attachment bitset/boolean logic. `git cat-file -p ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341` verifies its single parent 28ddfc88d8d547941c7f4713db527a3c2f9ec35a and the absent AI marker described above.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle starts in ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341, a single-parent 2009 implementation commit that first combined a count + 1 pointer array with two independently possible implicit-buffer appends. The older fake-front feature is not itself the BIC because its parent-era implementation could add only one element. Both -L and -S history converge on ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 for the exact need_real_front counter and allocation invariant, while 4fad615d689c61c6c3a000295a1fa755359737cb merely carries the same change onto the 1.6 stable line; there is no squash to decompose. The immediate parent tree directly lacks the real-front counter and second append, proving parent absence. The mechanism persisted through xorg-server-21.1.22. Direct fix b7aa65cc3bb11b792ce2a3f511ba9b863acb11c8 changed arithmetic counters to booleans/presence checks, and its child 339c279514326134b0878fc23ce6e9520440ce7f further deduplicated and bounded attachments; their release-branch equivalents are in xorg-server-21.1.23, matching the first-party patched boundary. Finally, attribution is judged only from the ff6c7764c2909e4126403b7211faa6c58556b341 commit object: it has a human author/committer and ordinary sign-off/review trailers, with no AI marker. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
